title: Backend Engineer
blurb: What a backend engineer should know, in the order to learn it: HTTP and OS basics, Node.js and TypeScript in depth, SQL and NoSQL, APIs, auth and security, caching, messaging, testing, architecture, DevOps, observability, system design and interview prep.
audience: Developers aiming for a backend or backend-heavy full-stack role

nodes.title: How the web and HTTP work
nodes.summary: Requests, methods, status codes, headers, caching, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3. Every backend answer sits on top of HTTP semantics, so this is the first thing interviewers probe.
checklist: Explain which HTTP methods are safe and which are idempotent, and why POST is neither
Pick the right status code for validation errors, conflicts, auth failures and rate limits (400, 409, 401 vs 403, 429)
Explain Cache-Control, ETag and conditional requests (If-None-Match, 304)
Compare HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 multiplexing and HTTP/3 over QUIC, including head-of-line blocking
Explain when to use WebSockets, server-sent events or long polling
Trace a request with curl -v and read every header in the response

nodes.title: DNS, TCP and TLS
nodes.summary: What happens between typing a URL and receiving bytes: name resolution, the TCP handshake, TLS and the latency each one adds.
checklist: Walk through recursive DNS resolution, record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT) and TTLs
Explain the TCP three-way handshake, retransmission, flow control and congestion control
Contrast TCP and UDP and say which protocols use each
Describe the TLS 1.3 handshake, certificates and the chain of trust
Estimate round trips for a cold HTTPS request and explain how keep-alive and connection reuse help
Explain ports, sockets and why a server can hold many connections on one port

nodes.title: Processes, threads and concurrency
nodes.summary: How the OS runs your code: processes, threads, scheduling, locks and non-blocking I/O. Explains why Node scales I/O on one thread and where it does not.
checklist: Explain process vs thread vs coroutine and what each shares (memory, file descriptors)
Describe a context switch and why it costs time
Explain race conditions, mutexes and semaphores, with a check-then-act example across awaits
List the four conditions for deadlock and one way to prevent each
Explain epoll/kqueue and how an event loop multiplexes thousands of sockets

links.title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces (free book)

nodes.title: Memory and file systems
nodes.summary: Virtual memory, the stack and heap, the page cache and how files hit disk. Needed to reason about memory leaks, OOM kills and fsync durability.
checklist: Explain virtual memory, paging and what a page fault is
Contrast stack and heap allocation and what garbage collection does to the heap
Explain the page cache and why a write() is not durable until fsync
Describe inodes, file descriptors and what happens when a process runs out of them
Explain blocking, non-blocking and async I/O, and mmap vs read/write

nodes.title: Linux and the command line
nodes.summary: Shell fluency and the handful of tools you use to debug a server: processes, logs, ports, disk and network.
checklist: Navigate, search and pipe text with grep, find, xargs, sort, uniq and jq
Inspect processes and resources with ps, top/htop, free, df and du
Find what is listening on a port with ss or lsof and test it with curl
Debug connectivity with ping, dig, traceroute and tcpdump
Manage permissions, environment variables, signals (SIGTERM vs SIGKILL) and SSH keys
Write a small bash script with set -euo pipefail

links.title: MIT: the missing semester of your CS education

sections.title: A backend language, deeply (Node.js and TypeScript)

nodes.title: JavaScript fundamentals
nodes.summary: Scope, closures, prototypes, promises and async/await. The language under every Node service and the source of most output-prediction questions.
checklist: Explain closures and lexical scope with a practical example (memoize, once)
Explain the four rules for `this` and how arrow functions change them
Walk the prototype chain and explain what `class` compiles to
Chain promises and handle errors with try/catch around await
Use Promise.all, allSettled, race and any, and say when each fits
Implement a concurrency-limited promise pool with retries

nodes.title: TypeScript
nodes.summary: Types, generics, narrowing and runtime validation on top of JavaScript. Strict TypeScript plus a schema library like zod is the default for new Node backends.
checklist: Model data with unions, intersections and discriminated unions
Write generic functions with constraints
Narrow `unknown` safely with type guards instead of using `any`
Use utility types (Partial, Pick, Omit, Record, ReturnType)
Validate request bodies at the boundary with zod and infer types from the schema
Configure tsconfig strict mode and explain what each strict flag catches

nodes.title: The Node.js event loop
nodes.summary: libuv, the event loop phases, microtasks and the thread pool. The single most asked Node interview topic and the key to not blocking your server.
checklist: Name the event loop phases (timers, pending, poll, check, close) and what runs in each
Predict the order of process.nextTick, promises, setTimeout and setImmediate
Explain what runs on the libuv thread pool (fs, dns.lookup, crypto, zlib) and UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE
Show how a CPU-heavy loop or JSON.parse of a huge body blocks every request
Measure event loop delay with perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay

links.title: Node.js: the event loop, timers and process.nextTick()
Node.js: don't block the event loop

nodes.title: Streams and buffers
nodes.summary: Readable, writable and transform streams with back-pressure. How you process large files and responses without loading them into memory.
checklist: Explain Buffers, encodings and why string concatenation of binary data breaks
Contrast readable, writable, duplex and transform streams
Explain back-pressure, highWaterMark and what write() returning false means
Use stream.pipeline (promise version) so errors and cleanup propagate
Stream a large CSV upload to the database without buffering it all in memory
Consume a stream with for await...of

nodes.title: Worker threads, cluster and Node performance
nodes.summary: Using more than one core, offloading CPU work and finding leaks and hot paths with profilers and heap snapshots.
checklist: Choose between worker_threads, child_process and cluster for a given workload
Move a CPU-bound task (image resize, hashing) to a worker pool
Explain why containers plus horizontal scaling often replace cluster in production
Profile CPU with --cpu-prof or clinic and read a flame graph
Find a memory leak by comparing two heap snapshots
Implement graceful shutdown on SIGTERM: stop accepting, drain, close pools

nodes.title: Express, Fastify and NestJS
nodes.summary: Routing, middleware, validation, error handling and dependency injection. Most Node backend jobs use one of these, and NestJS is common in larger teams.
checklist: Build an HTTP server with only the node:http module, then with a framework
Explain the middleware chain and write error-handling middleware
Structure a NestJS app with modules, controllers, providers and DI
Explain the NestJS request pipeline: middleware, guards, interceptors, pipes, filters
Connect to Postgres with a pool and explain ORM vs query builder trade-offs
Return consistent JSON errors without leaking stack traces

nodes.title: OOP, SOLID and design patterns
nodes.summary: Strategy, observer, factory, adapter and dependency injection. The vocabulary for low-level design rounds and for keeping services testable.
checklist: Explain each SOLID principle with a backend example
Prefer composition over inheritance and explain why
Implement strategy, factory, adapter and observer in TypeScript
Explain dependency injection and how it makes services testable
Spot common code smells and name the refactoring for each

links.title: Martin Fowler: inversion of control containers and DI

nodes.title: A second language (Go, Java or Python)
nodes.summary: Pick one to widen your options and to see how other runtimes handle concurrency. Useful, but not required to get hired as a Node engineer.
checklist: Write and test a small REST service in the second language
Explain its concurrency model (goroutines, JVM threads and virtual threads, or the Python GIL and asyncio)
Use its standard tooling: package manager, formatter, test runner
Compare its error handling with JavaScript exceptions

nodes.title: Git
nodes.summary: Branching, rebasing, resolving conflicts and recovering from mistakes. You will use it every day and be judged on clean history in code review.
checklist: Explain commits, branches and HEAD as pointers in a DAG
Choose between merge and rebase and explain what rebase rewrites
Resolve a merge conflict and continue a rebase
Recover lost work with reflog and undo safely with revert vs reset
Use interactive rebase to squash and reword before a PR
Find the commit that introduced a bug with git bisect

nodes.title: Code review, trunk-based development and feature flags
nodes.summary: How teams ship together: small PRs, useful review, short-lived branches and flags that separate deploy from release.
checklist: Write a PR description that explains why, how to test and the risk
Give review comments that focus on correctness, design and tests, not style
Explain trunk-based development vs long-lived feature branches
Use a feature flag to ship dark and roll out gradually, then remove it
Write commit messages that follow a convention such as Conventional Commits

nodes.title: SQL and relational modelling
nodes.summary: Queries, keys, constraints and normalisation. SQL is still the core skill for almost every backend role and a standard live-coding round.
checklist: Write SELECT with WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY and LIMIT
Explain NULL semantics (three-valued logic, COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col))
Choose primary keys (bigint, UUIDv7) and use foreign keys with ON DELETE actions
Normalise a schema to 3NF and explain when to denormalise
Use CHECK, UNIQUE and NOT NULL constraints so the database enforces invariants
Write an UPSERT with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT

nodes.title: Joins, CTEs and window functions
nodes.summary: The queries that separate juniors from mids: every join type, correlated subqueries, recursive CTEs and window functions for rankings and running totals.
checklist: Explain inner, left, full, self and cross joins and when a LEFT JOIN turns into an inner join
Write correlated subqueries and rewrite them with EXISTS or a join
Use CTEs and a recursive CTE to walk a tree (org chart, comments)
Use ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, LAG/LEAD and running SUM() OVER
Solve top-N per group and Nth highest salary
Write anti-joins (rows with no match) without NOT IN pitfalls on NULLs

nodes.title: Indexes
nodes.summary: B-trees, composite and covering indexes, partial and expression indexes. The first lever for a slow query and a favourite interview deep dive.
checklist: Explain how a B-tree index finds rows and why range scans work
Order columns in a composite index using the leftmost-prefix rule
Build a covering index for an index-only scan
Use partial and expression indexes for skewed data and lower(email) lookups
Explain when an index hurts: write cost, low selectivity, unused indexes
Create an index on a live table with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY

nodes.title: Query plans and query performance
nodes.summary: Reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE, join algorithms, statistics and the N+1 problem. How you prove why a query is slow instead of guessing.
checklist: Read EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) and find the most expensive node
Compare seq scan, index scan, index-only scan and bitmap heap scan
Explain nested loop, hash join and merge join and when the planner picks each
Spot row-estimate errors and fix them with ANALYZE or extended statistics
Detect and fix N+1 queries from an ORM
Use pg_stat_statements to find the queries worth optimising

nodes.title: Transactions and ACID
nodes.summary: Atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability, and how to use transactions correctly from application code.
checklist: Explain each letter of ACID with a concrete failure it prevents
Wrap a multi-statement change (transfer money) in a transaction from Node
Keep transactions short and never call external APIs inside one
Use SAVEPOINT and explain what happens to the connection after an error
Explain how the WAL gives durability and crash recovery

nodes.title: Isolation levels, MVCC and locking
nodes.summary: Dirty reads, lost updates, write skew and the locks or isolation levels that stop them. Where real concurrency bugs live.
checklist: Name the anomalies (dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom, lost update, write skew)
Say which anomalies Read Committed, Repeatable Read and Serializable prevent in Postgres
Explain MVCC: tuple versions, snapshots and why readers do not block writers
Prevent lost updates with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, atomic UPDATE or a version column
Retry serialization failures (SQLSTATE 40001) safely
Diagnose a deadlock from the Postgres log and fix lock ordering

links.title: Hermitage: testing isolation levels across databases

nodes.title: Schema migrations and zero-downtime changes
nodes.summary: Versioned migrations and the expand-and-contract pattern so schema changes never take the app down.
checklist: Run versioned, reviewed migrations with a tool (Prisma, Drizzle, Knex, Flyway)
Rename a column with expand, migrate, contract across several deploys
Know which ALTER TABLE operations take heavy locks and set lock_timeout
Backfill large tables in batches
Make every migration backward compatible with the previous app version

nodes.title: Postgres internals and operations
nodes.summary: Heap pages, VACUUM, the WAL, replication and connection pooling. What a senior engineer needs to keep Postgres healthy under load.
checklist: Explain dead tuples, bloat and what autovacuum does
Explain transaction ID wraparound and why it is dangerous
Describe streaming replication, read replicas and replication lag
Size a connection pool and explain PgBouncer transaction pooling
Plan backups and point-in-time recovery

nodes.title: NoSQL: documents, key-value and wide-column
nodes.summary: The main NoSQL families, what each is good at, and when MongoDB, Redis, DynamoDB or Cassandra is the right tool instead of Postgres.
checklist: Name the families (document, key-value, wide-column, graph, time-series) with one product each
Explain partition keys and sort keys in DynamoDB or Cassandra
Explain BASE vs ACID and what eventual consistency means for a read
Describe LSM trees and why they favour writes

nodes.title: MongoDB modelling and indexes
nodes.summary: Embed vs reference, schema patterns, compound indexes and the aggregation pipeline. The most common NoSQL database in Node stacks.
checklist: Decide embed vs reference from access patterns and document growth
Apply patterns such as bucket, subset, extended reference and computed
Order compound index fields with the equality, sort, range rule
Write an aggregation pipeline with $match, $group, $lookup and $unwind
Read explain() output and spot a COLLSCAN
Explain replica sets, read/write concerns and multi-document transactions

nodes.title: Redis
nodes.summary: Data structures, TTLs, persistence and the patterns built on them: caches, rate limiters, leaderboards, locks and queues.
checklist: Use strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets and streams for the right job
Set TTLs and explain eviction policies (allkeys-lru, volatile-ttl)
Build a sliding-window rate limiter with a sorted set or a Lua script
Explain RDB vs AOF persistence and what you can lose on a crash
Explain why a single-node SET NX lock is not safe for correctness

links.title: Martin Kleppmann: how to do distributed locking

nodes.title: Choosing a database
nodes.summary: A decision framework from access patterns, consistency needs, scale and team skills. Interviewers want a reasoned choice, not a favourite.
checklist: Start from access patterns, data shape and consistency needs, not hype
Defend Postgres as the default and name cases where it is the wrong choice
Explain OLTP vs OLAP and when to add a warehouse or columnar store
Know when search (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch) or a vector index belongs next to the main DB
Estimate data size and QPS to check a single node is enough

nodes.title: Distributed SQL
nodes.summary: CockroachDB, Spanner-style databases: SQL with automatic sharding and Raft replication. Worth knowing for global, high-availability systems.
checklist: Explain how ranges are split and replicated with Raft
Explain why multi-region writes add latency
Choose primary keys that avoid write hotspots
Handle transaction retry errors in application code

nodes.title: REST API design
nodes.summary: Resources, verbs, status codes, error shapes and webhooks. Designing a clean API is asked in almost every backend and system design loop.
checklist: Model resources and sub-resources with nouns and correct HTTP methods
Return consistent errors using RFC 9457 problem details
Use PUT vs PATCH correctly and explain their idempotency
Design filtering, sorting and field selection in query parameters
Design a webhook with signatures, retries and event ids
Handle long-running work with 202 Accepted and a status resource

links.title: RFC 9457: problem details for HTTP APIs

nodes.title: GraphQL and gRPC
nodes.summary: Alternatives to REST: GraphQL for flexible client queries, gRPC with Protobuf for fast typed service-to-service calls. Learn one deeply when a job needs it.
checklist: Write a GraphQL schema with queries, mutations and resolvers
Fix the N+1 problem with DataLoader batching
Protect a GraphQL API with depth/complexity limits and persisted queries
Define a Protobuf service and explain field numbers and backward compatibility
Compare unary and streaming gRPC calls and deadlines
Pick REST, GraphQL or gRPC for a given client and justify it

nodes.title: Pagination and filtering
nodes.summary: Offset vs cursor (keyset) pagination and stable sorting. A small topic with big performance consequences at scale.
checklist: Explain why OFFSET gets slower and skips or repeats rows under writes
Implement keyset pagination with a composite cursor (created_at, id)
Encode cursors as opaque tokens
Back the sort order with a matching index
Decide whether to return total counts and what they cost

links.title: Use The Index, Luke: no offset

nodes.title: API versioning and evolution
nodes.summary: Changing an API without breaking clients: additive changes, versioning schemes, deprecation and sunset.
checklist: List which changes are breaking and which are additive
Compare URL, header and date-based versioning
Explain Stripe-style version pinning with request/response transforms
Deprecate an endpoint with Deprecation and Sunset headers and usage metrics
Follow the robustness principle: tolerant readers, strict writers

links.title: Stripe: APIs as infrastructure, future-proofing with versioning

nodes.title: Idempotency and rate limiting
nodes.summary: Idempotency keys so retries are safe, and rate limits so one client cannot take the service down.
checklist: Implement an Idempotency-Key header that stores and replays the first response
Handle two concurrent requests with the same key
Compare token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window and sliding window limiters
Return 429 with Retry-After and rate-limit headers
Rate limit per user, per IP and per endpoint across many instances

links.title: Stripe: designing robust APIs with idempotency
Stripe: scaling your API with rate limiters
IETF draft: the Idempotency-Key HTTP header

nodes.title: API docs and contracts (OpenAPI)
nodes.summary: Describing your API in OpenAPI so docs, clients, mocks and contract tests come from one source of truth.
checklist: Write an OpenAPI 3.1 document with schemas, parameters and error responses
Choose spec-first or code-first and explain the trade-off
Generate a typed client from the spec
Lint the spec and fail CI on breaking changes

nodes.title: Authentication, passwords and MFA
nodes.summary: Proving who a user is: password hashing, MFA, passkeys, account recovery and brute-force protection.
checklist: Hash passwords with argon2id or bcrypt and explain salts and work factors
Explain why fast hashes (SHA-256) are wrong for passwords
Add TOTP MFA and explain why SMS is the weakest factor
Explain how passkeys (WebAuthn) resist phishing
Protect login with rate limits, lockout rules and generic error messages
Design a safe password-reset flow with single-use, expiring tokens

nodes.title: Sessions, cookies, CORS and CSRF
nodes.summary: Server-side sessions, cookie flags and the browser rules (same-origin, CORS, SameSite) that decide what an attacker can do.
checklist: Store a session id in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie and explain each flag
Rotate the session id on login to prevent fixation
Explain the same-origin policy and what CORS does and does not protect
Explain a CSRF attack and the defences (SameSite, tokens, Origin checks)
Revoke sessions on logout and password change

nodes.title: JWTs and token-based auth
nodes.summary: What a JWT is, how it is signed and verified, and the real trade-offs against sessions: revocation, size and storage.
checklist: Decode a JWT and explain header, payload and signature
Compare HS256 and RS256/EdDSA and when to publish keys via JWKS
Validate alg, exp, iss and aud, and reject alg none
Use short-lived access tokens with rotating refresh tokens
Explain why JWTs are hard to revoke and how to mitigate it

nodes.title: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect
nodes.summary: Delegated access and federated login: the authorization code flow with PKCE, scopes, ID tokens and the mistakes that lead to account takeover.
checklist: Explain the roles: resource owner, client, authorization server, resource server
Walk through the authorization code flow with PKCE step by step
Explain the difference between an access token and an OIDC ID token
Use state and nonce correctly and validate redirect URIs exactly
Choose client credentials for service-to-service calls
Explain why the implicit flow is deprecated

links.title: RFC 9700: OAuth 2.0 security best current practice

nodes.title: Authorization: RBAC, ABAC and ReBAC
nodes.summary: Deciding what an authenticated user may do. Broken access control is the top web risk, so it must be enforced on every request.
checklist: Explain authentication vs authorization
Compare RBAC, ABAC and relationship-based access (Zanzibar-style)
Prevent IDOR by scoping every query to the caller or tenant
Centralise policy checks instead of scattering if-statements
Write tests that prove a user cannot read another tenant's data

links.title: Zanzibar: Google's consistent, global authorization system

nodes.title: OWASP Top 10 and API security
nodes.summary: Injection, broken access control, SSRF, insecure design and the API-specific risks. Expect at least one security question in every backend loop.
checklist: Prevent SQL and NoSQL injection with parameterised queries and validation
Explain SSRF and defend an endpoint that fetches user-supplied URLs
Prevent mass assignment by allow-listing writable fields
Explain stored vs reflected XSS and output encoding from the backend side
Audit dependencies and pin versions to reduce supply-chain risk
Set security headers and limit request body size

nodes.title: Secrets and applied cryptography
nodes.summary: Keeping keys out of code, encrypting data in transit and at rest, and picking the right primitive for hashing, signing and encryption.
checklist: Load secrets from the environment or a secrets manager, never the repo or logs
Rotate a leaked key without downtime
Choose between hashing, HMAC, symmetric encryption and signatures
Use authenticated encryption (AES-GCM) and explain why nonces must not repeat
Explain envelope encryption with a KMS

nodes.title: Caching strategies
nodes.summary: Cache-aside, read-through, write-through and write-back, plus where to cache: in process, Redis, HTTP or CDN.
checklist: Implement cache-aside with Redis and a TTL
Compare read-through, write-through and write-back and their failure modes
Choose cache keys and TTLs and explain negative caching
Decide between an in-process LRU and a shared cache
Measure hit ratio and the latency a cache actually saves

links.title: AWS whitepaper: database caching strategies using Redis

nodes.title: Cache invalidation, stampedes and hot keys
nodes.summary: Keeping caches correct and stable: invalidating on writes, avoiding thundering herds and spreading hot keys.
checklist: Delete vs update the cache on write and explain the race in each
Prevent a cache stampede with request coalescing, locks or early refresh
Add TTL jitter so keys do not expire together
Handle hot keys with local caching or key splitting
Explain how Facebook keeps memcache consistent with leases

nodes.title: CDNs and HTTP caching at the edge
nodes.summary: Serving static and cacheable responses close to users, with the right Cache-Control headers and invalidation plan.
checklist: Explain how a CDN pull cache works and what the cache key contains
Set Cache-Control (max-age, s-maxage, stale-while-revalidate, private)
Version asset URLs instead of purging
Explain Vary and why it can wreck hit ratio
Decide what must never be cached at the edge

nodes.title: Queues and background jobs
nodes.summary: Moving slow or unreliable work out of the request path with a queue and workers: retries, backoff, dead-letter queues and scheduling.
checklist: Explain when to move work to a queue and what the user sees meanwhile
Run jobs with BullMQ or SQS and explain visibility timeouts and acks
Retry with exponential backoff and send poison messages to a DLQ
Schedule recurring jobs without running them twice across instances
Explain back-pressure and how to scale workers on queue depth
Explain at-most-once vs at-least-once delivery and make a consumer idempotent
Handle duplicate and out-of-order messages with dedup keys or versions

nodes.title: Kafka and event streaming
nodes.summary: A replicated log with partitions and consumer groups. The backbone for event-driven systems, CDC and analytics pipelines.
checklist: Explain topics, partitions, offsets and consumer groups
Choose a partition key to keep per-entity ordering
Explain replication, ISR and acks=all
Contrast a log (Kafka) with a queue (SQS, RabbitMQ)
Explain consumer lag and how to monitor it

nodes.title: Event-driven architecture and the outbox
nodes.summary: Services that react to events, choreography vs orchestration, and the transactional outbox that keeps the database and the event stream in sync.
checklist: Explain the dual-write problem when you save to the DB and publish an event
Implement a transactional outbox with a relay or CDC (Debezium)
Compare choreography and orchestration for a multi-step workflow
Design event schemas and version them
Explain the trade-offs: eventual consistency, harder debugging, replay

links.title: Martin Fowler: what do you mean by event-driven?

nodes.title: Testing fundamentals
nodes.summary: Unit tests, test doubles and the test pyramid or trophy. Testable code and a fast suite are what reviewers look for in take-home tasks.
checklist: Write fast unit tests for pure domain logic with Vitest or Jest
Explain mocks, stubs, fakes and spies and when mocking hurts
Explain the test pyramid vs the testing trophy
Test error paths and edge cases, not only the happy path
Run tests in CI and keep them deterministic (no real time, randomness or network)

links.title: Martin Fowler: the practical test pyramid
Kent C. Dodds: the testing trophy

nodes.title: Integration and contract tests
nodes.summary: Testing against a real database and real HTTP, and contract tests that catch breaking changes between services before deploy.
checklist: Run integration tests against a real Postgres with Testcontainers
Isolate tests with transactions or per-test schemas
Test an HTTP API end to end with supertest
Write a consumer-driven contract test with Pact
Explain where contract tests fit compared with end-to-end tests

nodes.title: Load and performance testing
nodes.summary: Finding the breaking point before users do: load, stress and soak tests, and reading latency percentiles.
checklist: Write a k6 script with thresholds on p95 latency and error rate
Explain load, stress, spike and soak tests
Explain why p99 matters more than the average
Find the bottleneck with the USE method (CPU, memory, DB, pool)

nodes.title: Monolith, modular monolith and microservices
nodes.summary: How to split a system and when not to. Includes API gateways and BFFs. A staple senior question about trade-offs, not fashion.
checklist: Explain the costs microservices add: network calls, data ownership, ops
Argue for a modular monolith first and say when to extract a service
Give each service its own data and avoid a shared database
Explain an API gateway and a backend-for-frontend
Explain service discovery and what a service mesh adds

nodes.title: Domain-driven design
nodes.summary: Bounded contexts, aggregates and a shared language with the business. The best tool for deciding service and module boundaries.
checklist: Explain bounded contexts and the ubiquitous language
Design an aggregate and explain why it is the transaction boundary
Distinguish entities and value objects
Map relationships between contexts (anti-corruption layer)

nodes.title: CQRS and event sourcing
nodes.summary: Separate read and write models, and storing state as a log of events. Powerful for audit-heavy domains, overkill for most CRUD.
checklist: Explain CQRS and when separate read models pay off
Explain event sourcing: append-only events, projections and snapshots
Handle event schema changes (upcasting)
Name the costs: eventual consistency and complexity

nodes.title: Resilience patterns
nodes.summary: Timeouts, retries with jitter, circuit breakers, bulkheads and load shedding: how a service survives its dependencies failing.
checklist: Set a timeout on every network call and propagate deadlines
Retry with exponential backoff and jitter, only on safe or idempotent operations
Explain how retries can cause a retry storm and how budgets prevent it
Implement a circuit breaker and explain its three states
Use bulkheads and load shedding to protect critical paths
Degrade gracefully when a non-critical dependency is down

links.title: AWS Builders' Library: timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter
AWS Builders' Library: using load shedding to avoid overload

nodes.title: Docker and containers
nodes.summary: Images, layers, multi-stage builds and running a Node service in a small, secure container.
checklist: Write a multi-stage Dockerfile for a Node app with a small runtime image
Order layers for good build caching
Run as a non-root user and handle signals (PID 1, tini or --init)
Use docker compose for a local app plus Postgres and Redis
Explain containers vs VMs (namespaces, cgroups)

nodes.title: CI/CD and deployment strategies
nodes.summary: Pipelines that test, build and ship on every merge, and rollouts that limit blast radius: rolling, blue-green and canary.
checklist: Build a GitHub Actions pipeline: install, lint, typecheck, test, build, deploy
Cache dependencies and run jobs in parallel
Compare rolling, blue-green and canary deployments
Roll back quickly and explain why database migrations complicate it
Keep secrets out of CI logs and use OIDC to the cloud instead of long-lived keys

nodes.title: The Twelve-Factor App
nodes.summary: Config in the environment, stateless processes, logs as streams and fast disposability. The baseline for anything that runs in the cloud.
checklist: Keep config in environment variables and validate it at startup
Make processes stateless so any instance can serve any request
Write logs to stdout as an event stream
Start fast and shut down gracefully (disposability)
Keep dev, staging and prod as similar as possible

nodes.title: Cloud primitives
nodes.summary: Compute, storage, networking and identity on a major cloud: VMs and containers, object storage, VPCs, load balancers and IAM.
checklist: Choose between VMs, containers (ECS, Cloud Run) and functions for a workload
Use object storage with presigned URLs for uploads
Explain VPCs, subnets, security groups and private databases
Write least-privilege IAM policies and use roles instead of keys
Use managed databases and explain multi-AZ failover
Declare infrastructure with Terraform or OpenTofu and explain state and drift

nodes.title: Kubernetes
nodes.summary: Pods, deployments, services and probes. Useful at scale; many teams have a platform group, but you should be able to deploy and debug on it.
checklist: Explain pods, deployments, services and ingress
Configure liveness, readiness and startup probes correctly
Set resource requests and limits and explain OOMKilled and CPU throttling
Use ConfigMaps and Secrets
Debug with kubectl get, describe, logs and exec
Explain the horizontal pod autoscaler

links.title: Kubernetes: configure liveness, readiness and startup probes

nodes.title: Serverless and edge functions
nodes.summary: Lambda, Vercel and Cloudflare Workers: pay-per-request compute with cold starts, time limits and connection-pool pitfalls.
checklist: Explain cold starts and what affects them
Handle database connections from functions (pooling proxies, HTTP drivers)
Know execution-time and payload limits and design around them
Decide when serverless is cheaper or more expensive than a container

nodes.title: Logs, metrics and traces
nodes.summary: The three signals and how they fit together to answer why production is slow or broken. Now expected of every backend engineer, not just SREs.
checklist: Explain what each signal is good for and what it costs
Correlate a log line, a metric spike and a trace with a shared trace id
Apply the RED method to services and the USE method to resources
Explain cardinality and why user ids do not belong in metric labels
Log structured JSON with a request id on every line (pino plus AsyncLocalStorage)
Redact secrets and personal data before logs leave the process

links.title: Google SRE book: monitoring distributed systems

nodes.title: Metrics and Prometheus
nodes.summary: Counters, gauges and histograms, PromQL and dashboards that show rate, errors and latency percentiles.
checklist: Choose counter, gauge or histogram for a measurement
Instrument request rate, error rate and latency histograms in Node
Write PromQL for rate() and histogram_quantile()
Follow metric naming and label conventions

nodes.title: Distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry
nodes.summary: Following one request across services with spans and context propagation, to find where the time goes.
checklist: Explain traces, spans, attributes and context propagation
Auto-instrument a Node service with the OpenTelemetry SDK
Propagate context through HTTP (W3C traceparent) and queues
Explain head vs tail sampling

nodes.title: SLOs, alerting and incident response
nodes.summary: Defining reliability targets, alerting on symptoms with error budgets, and running incidents and blameless postmortems.
checklist: Define SLIs and SLOs for an API and compute an error budget
Alert on burn rate instead of raw thresholds
Convert nines into allowed downtime per month
Run an incident: roles, communication, mitigation before root cause
Write a blameless postmortem with action items

links.title: Google SRE book: service level objectives
Google SRE workbook: alerting on SLOs

nodes.title: Scaling from one server to millions
nodes.summary: Stateless app servers behind a load balancer, read replicas, caches, queues and CDNs, added in the order the bottlenecks appear.
checklist: Explain vertical vs horizontal scaling and why stateless servers matter
Explain L4 vs L7 load balancing and health checks
Add read replicas and handle read-your-writes
Know the latency numbers every engineer should know
Do back-of-the-envelope estimates for QPS, storage and bandwidth

nodes.title: Replication and sharding
nodes.summary: Leader-follower and leaderless replication, partitioning strategies, consistent hashing and hot partitions.
checklist: Compare leader-follower, multi-leader and leaderless replication
Choose a shard key and explain range vs hash partitioning
Explain consistent hashing with virtual nodes
Handle hot partitions and resharding
Explain quorums (R + W > N)

links.title: Discord: how Discord stores trillions of messages

nodes.title: Consistency, CAP and distributed transactions
nodes.summary: Strong vs eventual consistency, CAP and PACELC, and sagas instead of two-phase commit across services.
checklist: Explain CAP precisely and why PACELC is more useful
Contrast linearizability, causal and eventual consistency
Explain two-phase commit and its blocking failure mode
Design a saga with compensating actions
Explain why distributed locks need fencing tokens

links.title: Martin Kleppmann: please stop calling databases CP or AP

nodes.title: System design fundamentals
nodes.summary: The building blocks put together: caching, queues, storage and trade-offs. Take the System Design roadmap next for full depth.
checklist: Run a design interview: requirements, estimates, API, data model, diagram, deep dives
Place caches, queues and CDNs in a design and justify each
State trade-offs out loud (consistency, cost, latency, complexity)
Identify single points of failure and add redundancy

nodes.title: System design case studies
nodes.summary: Practising the classic designs (URL shortener, feed, chat, rate limiter, payments) until the framework is automatic.
checklist: Design a URL shortener with key generation and read-heavy caching
Design a news feed and explain fan-out on write vs read
Design a chat system with WebSockets, ordering and offline delivery
Design a distributed rate limiter
Design a payment flow with idempotency and a double-entry ledger
Read two real architectures from company engineering blogs

links.title: System design primer: interview questions with solutions

nodes.title: Backend and Node deep-dive questions
nodes.summary: The conversational round: why Node is fast, when it is a bad fit, how you debug production and design APIs. Practise answering out loud.
checklist: Answer why single-threaded Node handles high concurrency and when it is a bad fit
Explain how you would debug a latency spike in production end to end
Walk through what happens when a request hits your API, from DNS to database
Explain a real concurrency bug you fixed or could hit
Solve one low-level design problem (LRU cache, rate limiter, parking lot) in TypeScript

nodes.title: DSA for backend interviews
nodes.summary: Hash maps, heaps, intervals and design-style coding problems that mirror backend work. Most loops still include at least one coding round.
checklist: Solve hash map and counting problems in under 20 minutes
Use a heap for top-K and scheduling problems
Merge and sweep intervals
Implement an LRU cache with a map and a doubly linked list
State time and space complexity for every solution

nodes.title: A production-grade portfolio project
nodes.summary: One deployed backend project with auth, a real database, a queue, tests, CI and observability. It gives you stories and proof for every round.
checklist: Build and deploy an API with auth, Postgres, migrations and pagination
Add a background job queue with retries and idempotent handlers
Add integration tests and a CI pipeline that blocks bad merges
Add structured logs, metrics and a dashboard, then load test it
Write a README with an architecture diagram and the trade-offs you made
Turn it into resume bullets with measured numbers

nodes.title: Behavioral stories and mock interviews
nodes.summary: STAR stories about ownership, conflict and failure, a project deep dive you can defend, and timed mock interviews to rehearse it all.
checklist: Write 8 STAR stories: conflict, failure, ownership, ambiguity, deadline, mentoring
Prepare a 5-minute project deep dive with architecture, decisions and metrics
Do at least two timed mock interviews and review the recording
Prepare answers to why this company and why you are leaving
